recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not recreate or edit the removed ValueSet extension spreadsheet for this issue; any separate naming cleanup should be handled under later ordinalValue-to-itemWeight issues rather than FHIR-8355.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core ValueSet issue asked that the ordinal value extension use decimal rather than integer because some survey instruments can have fractional scores.
initial_application: Jira records svn revision 5888. The migrated git commit e8c52f3a3682cb3dcbbc5b287c3949f7a201533f is the matching #8355 application and changes the old source/valueset/valueset-extensions-spreadsheet.xml ordinalValue row from integer to decimal.
additional_context: The old ValueSet extension spreadsheet is absent from current core. Later change-family work renamed ordinalValue to itemWeight and moved extension definitions to the FHIR Extension Pack; the retired ordinalValue and active itemWeight definitions both constrain Extension.value[x] to decimal. Current core also defines the itemWeight concept property with dataType decimal. A remaining Observation example comment mentions ordinalValue by name, but the actual examples use itemWeight with valueDecimal and the comment does not affect FHIR-8355's type-change request.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the original integer-to-decimal change is already present in history, the active current core replacement surface is decimal, and the moved external extension definitions are decimal.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive-with-Modification core issue renamed ordinalValue to itemWeight, explaining why current sources use itemWeight instead of the old extension name.

Later Published/Persuasive-with-Modification Vocab/FHIR-I issue added the itemWeight concept property with decimal datatype and removed terminology-resource contexts from the itemWeight extension; it was already represented on the combined branch.
